tasks.title: Record PostgreSQL hosting, cutover window and rollback decisions
tasks.objective: A decision record states D1-D5 options, recommended defaults, pending owner status and verified environment facts so backup, deploy and rehearsal work does not rest on guesses
tasks.estimate_rationale: Document plus read-only environment checks; no comparable execution history exists in this sandbox, so the estimate is preliminary
acceptance_criteria: Record lists D1 to D5 with options, recommended default and owner status pending or answered
Record states whether api.env sets TRAINING_BACKUP_DIR and the observed database and asset sizes
No decision is marked approved without an owner reference

verification.value: Read docs/decisions/TRAIN-6-postgres.md against the D1-D5 list in PLAN.md
verification.purpose: confirm every decision gate and environment fact is recorded
verification.expected: Five decisions with defaults and status plus backup dir, data size and disk facts

complexity.justification: Choices span hosting, availability window and rollback semantics that interact with deploy scripts

scope.justification: Produces one decision document and reads environment facts without code changes

duration.justification: Writing five decision entries and running read-only preflight style checks fits about an hour

risk.justification: A wrong hosting or rollback assumption propagates into irreversible cutover steps later

coupling.justification: Backup, deployment and rehearsal tasks consume these decisions directly

confidence.justification: Server-side api.env and production data volume are not visible in the repository

tasks.title: Add PostgreSQL store module with schema migration and readiness
tasks.objective: A new store module opens a pg pool from TRAINING_DATABASE_URL, applies schema 1 under an advisory lock, rejects newer schema versions and exposes an async readiness check while SQLite code stays intact
tasks.estimate_rationale: Mirrors the existing 50-line SQLite migrate/readiness module plus config, dependency and a test helper; no execution history to calibrate
acceptance_criteria: Running migration twice on an empty database creates projects and assets with TEXT ids, timestamps and data_json, INTEGER revision, schema_version and byte_size, and records version 1 once
A recorded schema version above 1 makes openPostgres reject with Unsupported database schema
assertPostgresReady rejects when version is not 1 or the server is unreachable
Production config throws when TRAINING_DATABASE_URL is missing and the URL is never logged
Test helper fails with an explicit message when TRAINING_TEST_DATABASE_URL is unset

verification.purpose: store module compiles beside unchanged SQLite code
schema, version guard and readiness behave as specified

complexity.justification: Type mapping must preserve exact strings and numbers, which needs some deliberate decisions

scope.justification: One new module plus config, dependency and helper; callers switch in a later task

duration.justification: Existing migrate and readiness logic is short, so porting it with tests takes about two hours

risk.justification: Wrong column types would silently alter API strings or hashes for every consumer

coupling.justification: Repository port, migration tool and backup all build on this schema module

confidence.justification: The source schema and config were read fully; PostgreSQL behaviour is standard

tasks.title: Port repositories, asset service, HTTP and WebSocket callers to PostgreSQL
tasks.objective: All runtime persistence uses the PostgreSQL pool through async methods while every status code, body, revision rule and publish-after-commit ordering matches the SQLite implementation
tasks.estimate_rationale: Six source files switch from sync to async with transaction semantics translated; no calibrated history, so estimate is moderate
acceptance_criteria: Ported repository test shows revision 1 on create, 2 on update and RevisionConflictError on stale revision
Unchanged update returns changed false, keeps revision and updatedAt and publishes no event
Stale expectedRevision on project update and import returns 409 REVISION_CONFLICT with stored currentRevision
Concurrent duplicate externalKey create maps unique violation to the same plain error and a 500 response
WebSocket upgrade for an unknown project still answers 404 and shutdown ends the pool

verification.purpose: all callers await the async persistence API
ported repository test passes on PostgreSQL

complexity.justification: BEGIN IMMEDIATE serialisation must become row locking without changing conflict outcomes across components

scope.justification: Touches repositories, service, HTTP handlers, WebSocket upgrade and server lifecycle

duration.justification: Mechanical async conversion plus careful mutate rewrite is roughly half a day

risk.justification: Clients depend on 409 bodies and revision numbers; a mistake loses edits or breaks sync

coupling.justification: Consumes the store module and defines the contract that parity tests and deployment use

confidence.justification: All persistence callers and error mapping were read; Express async forwarding remains assumed

tasks.title: Add HTTP parity and concurrency regression tests on PostgreSQL
tasks.objective: Executable HTTP-level tests prove client-visible responses and concurrent revision conflicts match the pre-migration contract on PostgreSQL
tasks.estimate_rationale: Two new test files driving createApp over an ephemeral port with a bearer token; uncalibrated estimate
acceptance_criteria: Tests assert create 201, get by id and external key, and 404 NOT_FOUND bodies
Stale PUT returns 409 with REVISION_CONFLICT and currentRevision; missing-key import with nonzero expectedRevision returns currentRevision 0
Unchanged import returns changed false; delete returns 204 and removes asset rows
readyz returns 200 normally and 503 after the version row is altered; invalid payload returns 400 VALIDATION_ERROR
Parallel PUTs with one expectedRevision yield exactly one success, the rest 409, final revision plus one

verification.purpose: HTTP parity and concurrency behaviour on PostgreSQL

complexity.justification: Expected outcomes are already defined by existing handlers; concurrency setup needs some care

scope.justification: Adds two test files without touching production source

duration.justification: Roughly a dozen HTTP cases plus a parallel writer harness takes about three hours

risk.justification: Weak assertions could let a regression in conflict handling pass unnoticed

coupling.justification: Tests consume the async repository contract produced by the port task

confidence.justification: createApp accepts an injected config with an MCP token, so tests can authenticate directly

tasks.title: Build verified SQLite-to-PostgreSQL data migration tool
tasks.objective: A CLI copies every projects and assets row verbatim from a read-only SQLite snapshot into empty PostgreSQL in one transaction and commits only when row counts and per-table SHA-256 hashes match
tasks.estimate_rationale: New CLI, shared hash module and fixture-based tests; two tables keep it bounded but verification logic needs care; uncalibrated
acceptance_criteria: Source failing integrity_check or not at user_version 1 aborts without writing
Non-empty or non-current target aborts without writing
Fixture with unicode, empty descriptions, large data_json and cascaded assets migrates with equal counts and hashes and a written report
Injected mismatch causes rollback, non-zero exit and an empty target
verify-only mode reports counts and hashes without writing

verification.purpose: migration commits on match and rolls back on mismatch
migration tool compiles against both drivers

complexity.justification: Hashing must be collation independent and byte exact across two different drivers

scope.justification: New CLI with its own hash module, npm script and dedicated test suite

duration.justification: Copy loop is small but fixtures, failure injection and report output need about four hours

risk.justification: A silent copy defect would lose or corrupt client training data at cutover

coupling.justification: Depends on schema module and its hash report is reused by backup verification

confidence.justification: Source schema has only two tables and was fully inspected

tasks.title: Replace SQLite backup with PostgreSQL dump and verified restore
tasks.objective: The backup command writes the existing directory layout with a pg_dump file and hash report, and a restore command restores a chosen backup into an empty database and proves counts and hashes match
tasks.estimate_rationale: Rewrite of a 24-line backup script, new restore script, Dockerfile client install and tests; client version depends on D1; uncalibrated
acceptance_criteria: Backup directory contains training.pgdump, assets, verification.json, checksums.sha256, git-sha.txt, schema-version.txt and manifest.json with store postgresql
pg_dump or pg_restore receive credentials through environment variables, never argv
A failed dump exits non-zero and leaves no manifest
Restore refuses bad checksums or a non-empty target and succeeds only when recomputed hashes match verification.json

verification.purpose: backup then restore round trip yields matching hashes
backup and restore compile into dist for the container

complexity.justification: External tool invocation with secret handling and checksum verification needs moderate design

scope.justification: Changes backup, adds restore, alters the container image and package scripts

duration.justification: Backup layout already exists, so rewrite plus restore and round-trip test fits three hours

risk.justification: Broken backups remove the only recovery path and may expose database credentials

coupling.justification: Reuses the migration hash report and depends on hosting decisions for client version

confidence.justification: Current backup flow was read; server-side backup dir and PostgreSQL version stay unresolved

tasks.title: Update deployment, cutover script and rollback guards for PostgreSQL
tasks.objective: Compose, deploy and rollback scripts support PostgreSQL and a guarded one-time cutover script migrates, verifies and activates or restores the old release, with docs describing runbook and restore
tasks.estimate_rationale: Edits three PowerShell scripts, adds one, updates compose and two docs; shape depends on D1-D3 owner answers; uncalibrated
acceptance_criteria: Compose keeps /app/data and /app/backups mounts and provides PostgreSQL per D1
deploy.ps1 refuses activation when PostgreSQL is unreachable or not at schema 1
cutover.ps1 takes a SQLite backup with the current release, runs verified migration and restarts the old release on any failure
rollback.ps1 refuses a pre-PostgreSQL release unless -AllowSqliteRollback is given and prints the data-loss warning
docs/deployment.md documents cutover, restore and rollback steps

verification.value: Review ops/ec2 scripts and docs, then execute them during the T8 rehearsal
verification.purpose: guards and runbook behave as specified on a non-production host
verification.expected: Each refusal path triggers and the success path activates the PostgreSQL release with readyz 200

complexity.justification: Failure branches must restore availability while sequencing backup, migration and activation

scope.justification: Spans compose, three existing scripts, one new script and deployment docs

duration.justification: Script edits are short but the new cutover sequence and docs need about two and a half hours

risk.justification: Mistakes here affect production availability and can lose writes after cutover

coupling.justification: Consumes the ported runtime and backup tooling and shares the release layout

confidence.justification: Script shape depends on unanswered hosting, window and rollback decisions
evidence: assumption:D1 D2 D3 owner answers pending

tasks.title: Rehearse cutover, restore and rollback on a production-like copy
tasks.objective: A rehearsal on a controlled host with a copy of a real backup demonstrates verified migration, API parity, backup restore and both rollback paths and records measured downtime
tasks.estimate_rationale: Execution time depends on unknown production data size and host setup; preliminary estimate only
acceptance_criteria: Rehearsal record shows migration report with equal counts and hashes for projects and assets
Record shows API test suite passing against the migrated copy
Record shows a backup restored into a fresh database with matching hashes and both rollback paths exercised
Record states measured write-freeze duration and confirms data copies were deleted

verification.value: Run cutover.ps1, restore and rollback.ps1 on a non-production host and fill docs/runbooks/TRAIN-6-rehearsal.md
verification.purpose: end-to-end product evidence for R1, R2 and R3
verification.expected: Hashes match, readyz 200 after cutover, restore verified, rollback paths behave and downtime recorded

complexity.justification: Coordinating several scripts on a realistic copy needs judgement when deviations appear

scope.justification: No product code changes; output is one rehearsal record

duration.justification: Three hours assumes small data volume and a ready host, both unverified

risk.justification: Copies include personal names, emails and ages, so mishandling exposes user data

coupling.justification: Depends on parity tests and deployment scripts being complete

confidence.justification: Host availability and dataset size remain unknown until decisions are answered

outputs: JSON report with per-table count and sha256
invariants: Rows sorted by id in JavaScript code-point order, not database collation
Each row serialized as a JSON array of columns in schema order with identical serializer for both stores
integration_criteria: Restore recomputes the report and matches verification.json written by backup

outputs: Unchanged status codes, bodies, revision numbers and project.revision events

Unchanged payload keeps revision and publishes no event
